newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet, diesel rally on regional demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet, diesel rally on regional demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and jet fuel on Thursday rallied on strong regional demand and talks of tightening supplies, traders said.

Gas oil demand was seen from China where a December cargo was sold at $1.65 premium to Singapore spot quotes on a c+f basis with another 40,000-tonne sold at 50 cents premium to spot quotes fob Singapore.One trader bid for 180,000-barrels at $30.90 a barrel fob Singapore, 40 cents more than Wednesday's traded level. December gas oil swaps held its ground despite an 84-cent drop in January Brent crude on Wednesday to trade at $30.20. The gas oil market also firmed on expectations India
may buy around 700,000-tonnes for January arrival against the 520,000-tonnes it bought for December.

Physical jet fuel traded at $31.95 a barrel, up 20 cents from Wednesday's traded level. The December jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) rose sharply and was last quoted at $1.45/$1.70 against Wednesday's bid at $1.25 a barrel. January regrade also rose and was quoted at $1.80/$2.00 from a day earlier's $1.40/$1.70.
Fuel oil firmed on talks of reduced North Asian supplies as China had bought up all available spot cargoes traders said. In Singapore a 20,000-tonne cargo traded at $123.50 a tonne.

Naphtha dipped on weaker overnight crude but fundamentals were still bullish on good demand for prompt cargoes. Traders said one one Japanese end-user was still uncovered for second-half December but traders remain long in January.

In Singapore, traders assessed premiums around $1.00 over Singapore quotes on a 9-conversion but no deals were reportedTaiwan awarded its 1997 buy term tender for 360,000 tonnes of N+A at $3.45 a tonne over Singapore quotes c-and-f Kaohsiung to an aggressive Swiss trader. Taiwan said it may consider a second contract.
